question: In the hidden map Bishui Cave (璧水洞), when the player challenges the boss "Bishui Golden-Eyed Beast," why does the player not enter the Burning status effect after being hit by a fire attack at the beginning?
reference_answer: Because the player initially used the Magic Treasure (法宝) Fire Shield (避火罩), which grants immunity to fire damage.

db_evidence.notes: Exhaustive sql search across semantic_triples, topic_facts, event_steps, object_states, episodes, visual_clips, and entities for '避火罩' (and the near-synonym '辟火罩') returns zero rows anywhere in the day-timeline memory DB. The only fire-related, time-proximate fact the DB does contain is a topic_facts/semantic_triples entry at 73740s describing the player inspecting the 业火杖 (Karmic Fire Staff) weapon-forging panel, which lists 'fire resistance 10+' as one of its stats. This is a plausible-sounding but incorrect distractor that every rollout converged on. The true clue interval (73780-73788) itself has no episodes/topic_facts/object_states rows in the DB describing a Fire Shield item use; frames pulled directly from the video at 73778-73785s show the player being fully engulfed in fire with no burn status appearing, and a nearby item/spell radial menu (龙光倍力丸, 保命丹, 如意画轴, 缩地青符 / 铜头铁臂, 定身法, 金蝉, 身外身法) that does not list 避火罩 by name, consistent with the Fire Shield having been activated earlier/off-screen rather than during the visible clue window itself.

root_causes: The Fire Shield (避火罩) magic-treasure usage is not captured anywhere in the memory database (no episode caption, topic_fact, semantic_triple, or object_state mentions it), so no amount of correct-term text search (rollouts 1 and 2 tried the exact right query) can retrieve it.

The DB does contain a superficially fire-and-resistance-related distractor (业火杖 weapon fire-resistance stat) at almost the same time (73740s, just before the clue window at 73780-73788), which every rollout picked up and used as its causal explanation instead.

clip_qa windows in 4/5 rollouts covered 73740-73830, which does include the true clue interval, but the visual sub-agent read the weapon-forging panel and HP/hit frames rather than identifying any Fire Shield buff/immunity cue, so even direct visual access did not recover the reference fact.

Rollout 3 additionally mislocalized in time, running clip_qa on 70740-70800 and 74040-74120, neither of which is the 73780-73788 clue window, compounding the missing-evidence problem with a retrieval-window error.

Judge scoring is noisy at the margin: rollout 0 and rollout 4 submitted essentially the same wrong (业火杖-based) explanation and were scored 0 and 1 respectively, suggesting some of the score spread reflects judge inconsistency rather than a genuine difference in answer quality.
what_worked: Rollouts 1 and 2 correctly hypothesized the right kind of item (a fire-proofing magic treasure) and issued semantic_search queries using plausible Chinese terms (辟火罩/避火罩) directly targeting it — good query formulation that was defeated only by the fact genuinely being absent from the DB.
Most rollouts (0,1,2,4) correctly localized the clue window in time (~73700-73900s, close to true clue_interval 73780-73788) via run_sql time-range scans and pointed clip_qa at that region.
All rollouts correctly identified that a fire hit occurs without a subsequent burning-status indicator, i.e. they got the phenomenon right even though they got the mechanism wrong.
transferable_lessons: When a text search for the exact expected causal item comes back empty in every table (as rollouts 1 and 2 confirmed), treat that as evidence the retrievable evidence may be incomplete rather than immediately substituting the nearest fire-themed fact found elsewhere as the answer — flag lower confidence or note the alternative was not visually confirmed as an active buff.

For 'why does status X not occur' causal questions in this game, the mechanism is often an item/buff use that precedes the observed moment; agents should widen the visual/text search further backward in time (not just the exact clue window) to look for an item-activation event before the hit, not only inspect stats visible right at the hit.

clip_qa should be prompted to specifically scan for buff/status icons (e.g., near the HP bar or a temporary shield icon) rather than only reading equipment panels, since the panel it fixated on (业火杖 forging stats) was a red herring that was visually salient but causally irrelevant.

Near-identical wrong answers can receive different judge scores (0 vs 1 here); do not treat a single low-effort judge call as fully reliable at the pass/fail boundary for causal-reasoning questions with this much detail.
